title: Compact cost cards: keyboard navigation and RTL readiness audit
creator: Maya Singh
description: Goal: ship a low-density/compact presentation mode for cost cards used across Cost Overview and Rollouts dashboards while ensuring keyboard-first interactions, screen-reader semantics, and bidirectional language (RTL) readiness. The compact cards are targeted for customers using dense dashboards on small screens and for users who prefer reduced vertical space. This ticket covers design updates, accessibility fixes (WCAG AA target for normal text, AA/AAA checks for UI controls), keyboard focus flows, and an i18n sweep (text truncation, mirroring, numeric formats).
acceptance_criteria: Compact cost cards render correctly at three breakpoints: 320px, 768px, 1024px
All interactive elements reachable via keyboard in a logical order; focus ring visible and meets contrast requirements
Screen reader reads meaningful label + concise content summary for each card (title, 1-line description, cost metric) using aria-labelledby/role="region" patterns
Background and foreground color combinations meet WCAG AA contrast ratio >= 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large numeric values (>= 18pt/14pt bold)
RTL mirrored layout preserves ordering of controls and does not truncate localized strings; numeric and currency formats respect locale
Design tokens used (color, spacing, focus) so engineering can toggle between dense and default modes without duplicated CSS
comments: 2026-02-22 Maya Singh: Initial wireframes posted to Figma. I focused on single-line metrics and an optional chevron to expand detail. Requested engineering input on preferred semantic DOM structure for screen readers.
2026-02-25 Liam Ortega: Reviewed keyboard flow. Suggested adding a skip-to-cards link on pages where dense mode is default. Noted potential issue with focus trap inside the card expansion panel.

2026-03-01 Accessibility review (Anika Patel): Ran Lighthouse + axe-core on prototype. Found 3 issues: insufficient focus contrast on compact link buttons, missing aria-expanded on chevrons, and truncated RTL labels in Spanish (es-ES) when long metric names are present.

2026-03-04 Engineering (Marco Liu): Implemented tokenized focus ring and updated CSS variables for compact spacing. Raised PR #5412. Called out performance considerations for continuous rendering of large lists when focus outline is thick; suggested a 2px focus ring using color token 'focus-strong' instead of 3px.

2026-03-08 PM review (Jesse Park): Prioritized keyboard fixes and i18n rollup for beta customers next sprint. Requested that we not ship compact mode by default until contrast and screen reader semantics are confirmed.

2026-03-11 Design QA (Maya Singh): Ran manual keyboard pass with VoiceOver and NVDA. Confirmed aria-labelledby pairing but discovered that expansion chevrons announce as 'button' with no context. Updated designs to include aria-label template: '{metric} details, press enter to expand'.

2026-03-12 Engineering (Liam Ortega): Implemented aria attributes and updated CSS variables. PR #5480 includes RTL mirroring utilities and a utility to format numbers via Intl.NumberFormat. Added unit tests for focus order and snapshot tests for RTL layout.
decisions: Use a single compact token set: spacing-compact, font-compact, focus-compact to reduce duplication in CSS and make toggling simple for eng ops
Adopt a 2px focus ring using token 'focus-strong' with color that meets 4.5:1 contrast against the nearest background to balance accessibility and visual density

Chevron expanders will be semantics-first: role=button, aria-expanded, aria-controls; visible label for screen readers using aria-label template; expanded content rendered immediately in DOM (no inert) to preserve reading order
Numbers and currencies will be formatted via Intl.NumberFormat with a locale prop exposed from console locale; avoid manual truncation of numeric suffixes in design—allow wrapping where needed
RTL mirroring will use CSS logical properties and avoid absolute left/right offsets to reduce layout regressions
next_steps: Finish a11y fixes in PR #5480 and get eng review from accessibility team (Anika)
Run automated accessibility regression suite across supported locales (en-US, fr-FR, es-ES, ar-SA) and report failures to this ticket
Design to provide updated token table and a11y checklist entries for Console Design System (Maya)
Schedule 1-hour beta preview with two customer accounts using dense dashboards (Ops team to coordinate)
Incorporate feedback and prepare release notes for console-2026.03 if no regressions are found
